threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘Wick’ in Hackney refers to the high street, not the trendy new bars. Classic rookie mistake.
Caught a lad trying to bribe the driver with a half-eaten donut last night on the 322. Not sure if it was the 3am vibe or just Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard someone argue about the best döner in the area while waiting for the U-Bahn, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night bakery where the queue for fresh Brez'n snakes down the street, just past a techno club's thumping bass.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell when someone’s from here if they know not to trust a BART announcement. Delays are a way of life, not just a heads-up.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo trying to get his suitcase up the bus steps. Everyone was cool about it, like this was an everyday occurrence.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all Gaudí and tapas; they miss the quiet corners with local artists painting in the shade and kids playing in hidden squares.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still refer to the metro as the 'subway' and can’t figure out the difference between vermut and gin. Classic signs, really.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a supermarket instead of a 'shop' and think it's normal to wear trainers at the pub.
Last night on the 77, a guy started reciting Shakespeare to a packed bus. The only one who clapped was the driver. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid on a bike, dodging potholes like it was a video game, while the kebab shop next door blared Turkish pop. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst at 3 AM after dancing at a club, then hear a spontaneous street concert while waiting for the bus.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know to avoid BART delays like the plague, but still can’t resist a burrito at 10 PM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy in a full suit juggle three oranges on the 19 while the bus hit every pothole on Larkin. Classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars close early, but it’s the locals who keep them open till dawn, sharing secrets only we know.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle with the 'T' and 'D' on the Metro maps. Locals glide seamlessly through the labyrinth.
